Scan the Zig source of a package for exported functions

Source: R/scan.R
scan_exports.Rd

Reads src/rzig/src/main.zig, and every Zig file that it imports with pub const name = @import("file.zig"); (recursively), and lists every public top-level Zig function whose documentation comment contains a line /// @export. A function of an imported file is registered as name.function; its R name is the function name. /// @export above pub const twice = other.twice; re-exports a function of a file imported as other under the name twice. A file imported with a plain const cannot be reached by the generated registration, so a marker in it is an error; a marked file that is not imported at all is ignored, and rzig_status() notes it. R names must be unique across all files.

Usage

scan_exports(path)

Arguments

path

Path to a package previously initialized with use_rzig().

Value

An object of class rzig_exports: a list with one element per exported function, each a list with name (the R function name), identifier (the Zig identifier as written), parameters (the R argument names), parameter_types (the Zig types of the R arguments), return_type (the Zig return type as written), doc (the documentation comment without the @export line), line (the line of the declaration), internal (TRUE for /// @export internal) and file (the file below src/rzig/src), invisible and defaults (a named character vector of R expressions). The attributes package, path, source (the entry file), files (every file scanned) and unreachable (marked files that main.zig does not import) record where the exports come from. as.data.frame() turns the object into a table with one row per function.

Details

The marker line takes options: /// @export internal registers the function without exporting its R wrapper, /// @export invisible makes the wrapper return its value invisibly, and /// @export name=<R name> gives the wrapper an R name other than the Zig name. Lines /// @default <argument> <R expression> give default arguments of the wrapper, for example /// @default tolerance 1e-8. A line /// @export internal registers the function and generates its R wrapper without exporting the wrapper from the package, for native routines that the package's own R code calls. The scan is pure R and needs no Zig compiler; the Zig compiler checks the parameter and return types when the package is installed.

A struct whose documentation comment contains /// @class becomes an R class: its pub fn init is the constructor, exported under the name of the struct, and every public function whose first parameter is the struct (self: *T, self: *const T or self: T) is a method, registered as the internal routine T_method and called as x$method(...) on an object x. Objects are rzig.External values (see the README); deinit, when declared, runs when R collects the object.

A function is found when its declaration starts at the beginning of a line with pub fn and the lines directly above it are /// documentation comments (blank lines and ordinary // comments between the comment block and the declaration are ignored). The first parameter is omitted from the R signature when its type is *rzig.Ctx.

Examples

package_path <- tempfile("rzig-scan-", tmpdir = tempdir())
dir.create(package_path)
writeLines(c("Package: examplepkg", "Version: 0.0.1"),
  file.path(package_path, "DESCRIPTION"))
use_rzig(package_path)
#> Generated RZig bindings for examplepkg: 1 exported function
#> Created RZig scaffold for package examplepkg
exports <- scan_exports(package_path)
exports
#> Zig exports of package examplepkg (src/rzig/src/main.zig): 1 function
#> 
#> hello_zig(name)
#>   name       []const u8             character, length 1, copied
#>   returns    rzig.Error![]const u8  character, length 1
as.data.frame(exports)
#>        name arguments           return_type documented internal line
#> 1 hello_zig      name rzig.Error![]const u8       TRUE    FALSE   17
unlink(package_path, recursive = TRUE)
